description.p: Drift is a free desktop video editor that feels simple from the first cut. Drop in video, photos, and music, add effects and stickers, generate captions automatically, and export — no subscription, no watermark, and no account required.
Great for social videos, explainers, and everyday projects. Cut subjects out of a frame, animate to the beat, style text and shapes, then add fonts and stickers only when you need them.

ul.li: Multi-track timeline — trim, split, snap, and undo as you go
Effects, transitions, and reusable look templates
Stickers, emoji, titles, and shapes for a finished look
Auto captions from speech in your video
Cut out subjects, mask clips, and key out green screens
Speed changes, reverse playback, and fades
Animate to the beat of your music
Mix audio and clean up background noise
Optional addons for fonts, stickers, and extras
Project bundles that keep your media together

description.p: Text and shapes are redrawn through Skia with layered styles, gradients and a new animation engine, Lottie and SVG clips arrive on the timeline, over a hundred new transitions land in the add-ons catalog, and Windows gets a Direct3D zero-copy path with fixes for NVIDIA stutter.

ul.li: Text styles: fill, stroke, shadow, glow and extrude layers with solid, gradient, texture or shader paints, a Looks gallery (Neon, Chrome, Holographic, Glitch, Outline, Echo and more), curved baselines and keyframable size, tracking and layer settings

Text animations: per-character, word or line animators with In, Out and Loop preset galleries — typewriter, type-on blur, rise by word, snap together, glitch, flicker, colour wave, wipe, karaoke pop and bounce, and 40 more
Shapes share the same style stack: gradient fills, multiple strokes, shadows, glows and dashes, all keyframable so shapes can animate
Lottie (.lottie, .json) and SVG files import as vector clips, with a Motion inspector for editing slots, playback options and poster frames
100+ new GPU transitions ported from gl-transitions, available through the add-ons catalog, plus easing curves for every transition
In-app Marketplace for browsing and downloading stock media, with a separate download-queue window
Adjustment layers in the Effects tab; masks are now keyframeable adjustment layers with on-canvas handles and their own Masks tab
Cutouts via Robust Video Matting, and Paste Attributes with selective picking across multi-clip selections

Windows: Direct3D 11 zero-copy decoding and a GPU switcher for hybrid laptops; fixed CUDA zero-copy and CUDA/OpenGL interop stutter on NVIDIA, hybrid-GPU decode, display-cadence stutter and the black preview on software OpenGL; new playback diagnostics and a warning for hardware-acceleration settings that will not work on the current machine
Audio: multi-channel waveform view, decibel volume control, multi-track audio extraction, and separate-audio / unlink actions on the timeline

Media bin: tree view, Import Folder, nested folder moves, multi-select with Shift-click ranges and bulk actions, safe removal of in-use media, lossless 90° rotation correction and non-destructive trimming from the bin
Android: hardware-accelerated video decoding and a reworked mobile layout
Save As, track renaming, select-all-and-move, keyboard delete, Shift+Arrow frame-by-frame scrubbing, native shortcut labels on macOS, and settings moved into a dialog
MCP: headless CLI mode, text, shape and motion-graphics tools, and lower token usage
Translations: Tagalog and Vietnamese added; Japanese and Spanish updated

description.p: Thanks to @jmn8718 for lossless rotation correction, Import Folder, track renaming and the media bin multi-select and folder moves; to @gorio for safe media removal, keyboard delete, separate-audio and unlink actions, track numbering and native macOS shortcuts; to @TSFBCE24RhythmHeaveners for the Tagalog translation; to @tojidotakarin for Vietnamese; to @coolvitto for Japanese; and to @angelreyesvelazquezjesus-gif for Spanish.
A quick bug-fix release for NVIDIA users. If playback looks fine on your machine, you can skip this update.

ul.li: Fixed black flicker between frames during NVIDIA hardware-decoded preview.

description.p: This is the first public release of Drift for Android. On the desktop, preview and export stay on the GPU, the media bin gets folders, and Face Swap, video stabilization, and several new languages land in this version.

ul.li: First public Android app — edit on a phone with a touch UI, including crop and trim from the bin, and AV1 playback
Preview stays on the GPU instead of copying every frame through the CPU, so Full / Half / Quarter match the preview panel size
Export converts frames to the encoder format on the GPU; typical 8-bit exports are faster
Folders in the media bin: create, rename, nest, and move clips between them
Preview, trim, and crop a clip from the bin before putting it on the timeline
Face Swap effect: replace a face in a clip with a still photo
Video stabilization to smooth camera shake, with a smoothness slider and optional tripod lock
Settings → Interface scale (100–200%), and a first-launch language chooser
Timeline scroll pans left and right, Shift+scroll moves between tracks, and middle-click drag also pans
Closing a project with unsaved changes now asks Save / Don't Save / Cancel
Translations: Brazilian Portuguese, Chinese (Simplified), French (Canada), Spanish, Italian, and Sinhala

description.p: Thanks to @CathodeAnode for the French (Canada) translation, SVG icons, translatable UI strings, and restoring a maximized window after fullscreen on KDE; to @yosenstar for Chinese (Simplified); to @alexbassani for Brazilian Portuguese; to @roger-fernandes-Dev for timeline scroll and pan; and to @jmn8718 for folders in the media bin.
GPU decoding and encoding on every platform, effect and text presets you can reuse across projects, and a fix for NVIDIA on Wayland.

ul.li: Fixed the black preview on NVIDIA under Wayland — Drift now runs as a native Wayland app instead of falling back to X11
Video decoding for the preview now uses the GPU on Windows and macOS too, not only Linux, and you can pick the backend from the preview toolbar
Export can encode on the GPU with NVENC, Quick Sync, AMF, VAAPI or VideoToolbox
Copy an effect or a whole effect stack between clips, and save your own presets
Save the look of a title as a text style and reuse or share it
The subtitle editor follows the playhead, and titles can contain colour emoji
Save a project as readable JSON and open one back again
Close a gap on a track, or split just one clip instead of every clip under the playhead
Window size and panel proportions are remembered between sessions
A bug button in the header collects the details needed for a good bug report
Large media imports are faster and use far less memory

description.p: Thanks to @CathodeAnode for the NVIDIA Wayland fix and the media-library performance work, and to @jmn8718 for close gap and per-clip split.
A big update with macOS support, AI agent control, new editing tools, and a batch of everyday fixes.

ul.li: Added MCP support — you can now let AI agents like Claude Code control the editor
Improved macOS support, including a working video preview
.drift project files now open with the editor when you double-click them
Cut a multi-camera shoot by watching every camera at once and switching between them
Find scenes inside a clip and jump straight to them
New 3D Face Mesh effect that follows the face through the clip
Mark an In and Out on the timeline to play and export just that range
Export short clips as animated GIFs
A portrait layout for vertical videos, with the preview on top
Zoom and pan the preview; drag or delete keyframes on the graph
Choose 1440p when setting up a project
Windows releases include a portable zip that needs no installer
Pick a language in Settings — More languages coming soon
Choose how many words go in each auto-generated caption
Fixed lag and audio going out of sync when two clips from the same file overlap
Fixed silent playback on some Windows audio devices
Phone videos keep their portrait size instead of becoming a square
Transitions no longer reset when you click them
Scrolling over a slider no longer also scrolls the panel behind it
Starting a new project now fully clears the previous one

description.p: A quick bug-fix release for AppImage users only. If you installed Drift from Flathub, the Arch package or the Windows installer, nothing changes for you and there is no need to update.

ul.li: Videos that the AppImage refused to open, or played as a black picture, now work. The AppImage was bundling a cut-down copy of FFmpeg that didn't have several codecs.
The AppImage now runs natively on Wayland instead of falling back to XWayland. The Wayland platform plugin was missing from the bundle.

description.p: A polish release focused on export options, playback controls, and everyday editing quality-of-life.

ul.li: Export at different frame rates, including audio-only export
Export freeze frames as images; remember last export folder and settings
Playback controls for navigating the timeline
Animation tab with custom editable fade curves
Persist dark mode and media view; option to reopen the last project at startup
Timeline zoom stays centered on the playhead or cursor
Close gaps when trimming; clearer trim start/end icons
Avoid color-space conversion during composition that could reduce quality

description.p: A feature release with new editing tools, timeline and asset-browser improvements, UI polish, performance work, and a batch of bug fixes.

ul.li: Aspect-locked clip resize in the preview (hold Shift to stretch freely)
Type exact values into property sliders; drag from the slider head works reliably
Delete, rename, search, favorites, and category browsing in the asset panel
Replace media in place while keeping timeline clips, effects, and layout
Disable and reorder effects on a clip; beauty and makeup face effects
Audio tempo follows clip speed; reverse video builds a reverse proxy with progress
Freeze frame captures the full composited image; clearer timeline bookmarks
Fit timeline in view, wider zoom for long projects, and scrolling on smaller screens
Redesigned text properties panel and style packs in the Text assets tab
Prompt to install essential addons on startup; less intrusive update notifications
Reliable media drag-and-drop onto the timeline on Mutter / GNOME
Fixed file-picker extensions on Flatpak, subtitle cue waveforms, and the project setup dialog
Faster filmstrip thumbnails and lighter subtitle voice waveform mixing

description.p: Fixes for saving and exporting through the desktop file picker.

ul.li: Saving a project or exporting without typing a file extension no longer leaves the result as a hidden file in flatpak builds

description.p: A small fix-up release on top of the first public version.

ul.li: Curves in the keyframe editor are drawn sharply instead of blurred

description.p: The first public release of Drift — a free, open-source desktop video editor with no subscription, no watermark and no account.

ul.li: Multi-track timeline with trim, split, snap, ripple and full undo
GPU effects, transitions and reusable look templates
Titles, shapes, stickers and emoji
Automatic captions from the speech in your video
Subject cutout, clip masks and green-screen keying
Speed changes, reverse, fades and beat-synced animation
Audio mixing, an effect chain and background noise removal
Project bundles that keep a project and its media together
Export to MP4 (H.264 + AAC) that matches the preview
Optional addons for fonts, stickers, speech models and acceleration runtimes
